sections.text: Always write the brand as 'Inkloom': one word, capital I only. Never 'InkLoom', 'Ink Loom' or 'INKLOOM'.
Avoid hype terms such as 'revolutionary', 'game-changing' or 'disruptive'. Show, don't shout. Describe what the product does in plain, specific language.
Use at most one exclamation mark per piece. Avoid pressure tactics such as 'hurry', 'ASAP' or false deadlines.
Prefer neutral terms: 'everyone' not 'guys', 'workforce' not 'manpower', 'chair' not 'chairman', 'remarkable' not 'crazy' or 'insane'.

Link text must describe the destination, for example 'Read the pricing guide', never 'click here'. Every image needs alt text. Aim for a reading level of grade 9 or below and keep sentences under 30 words.
Do not promise guaranteed outcomes unless a written warranty applies. Words such as 'guaranteed' or 'always' need legal sign-off.
Superlatives (best, #1, 100%) must reference an independent, dated source.
Any 'free' offer must state its terms or link to them within the same view.
Comparisons with named competitors must cite a dated, independently verifiable study. Do not disparage competitors.
